title: MEAT AT TWILIGHT, BREAD AT DAWN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The LORD said to Moses, 'I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell
them, "At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with
bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God."'" - Ex 16:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is that refrain again: "Then you will know that I am the LORD your God."

It has run through the whole book. Pharaoh was to know it. Egypt was to know it.
Now Israel is to know it, and the means is a meal.

That is worth pausing on. God revealed Himself to Egypt through plagues and to
Israel through dinner. The same purpose, very different methods. He knows what
each situation requires.

Notice how ordinary the revelation is. Meat in the evening, bread in the
morning. No thunder, no earthquake. Just food arriving reliably, day after day.

Many of us are waiting for a dramatic experience of God while missing the daily
evidence. The meal on the table, the strength for the day's work, the sleep that
came, the friend who called. God has been feeding you.

Jesus taught His disciples to notice this. He pointed to birds that neither sow
nor reap, and to wildflowers dressed better than Solomon, and said, "how much
more will he clothe you" (Matt 6:30).

You may know God better through your kitchen than through anything spectacular.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What ordinary provision have you stopped noticing?
2. Are you waiting for a dramatic sign while ignoring daily evidence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, open my eyes to the ordinary ways You provide for me every day. Thank You
for food, breath, and strength that I take for granted. Amen.
